summary: Loads and plays back Alembic geometry sequences, including polymeshes, curves, points, transforms, object-path selection, and standard or custom attributes.

key_params.name: objectpath
key_params.note: Object or hierarchy inside the archive to load; can load all objects

key_params.name: time
key_params.note: Playback time into animated Alembic data

key_params.name: timeunit
key_params.note: Interpret Time in frames, seconds, or other supported units

key_params.name: interp
key_params.note: Interpolate dynamic geometry when transform information is present

key_params.name: straightgpu
key_params.note: Load directly to GPU for speed

key_params.name: loadfile
key_params.note: Unload/reload the archive so external tools can overwrite it

common_gotchas: Straight to GPU mode is fast but prevents downstream SOP use and SOP-to-DAT/CHOP geometry access.
Bake normals and UVs into the Alembic file when using GPU direct mode, because downstream SOPs cannot add them.
When objects have different attribute sets in GPU direct mode, missing attributes receive default values.
The official xform menu uses repeated transform ids for several labels, so keep label context when documenting it.
key_concepts: Alembic SOP loads Alembic geometry sequences including polymeshes, curves, points, transforms, and attributes.
The objectpath parameter selects all geometry or a specific object/hierarchy inside the archive.
Animated archives are sampled with time and timeunit controls, with interpolation available for dynamic geometry that includes transform information.
Straight-to-GPU mode is faster but prevents normal downstream SOP access to the loaded geometry.
